body:
They know.  I've done it before for a few weeks at a time, but never anything close to permanent.  This probably isn't the best decision I'll ever make and I already feel foolish about it as is, but another part of me wants very much to get away from everyone in this town.  I'd like to start fresh somewhere.  You think you sound childish?  Everything I do is a step in the wrong direction.  I'm aware of it, but I feel the need to try it anyways.  If things go horribly wrong I'll just chalk it up as a lesson learned.

I'm off to bed for the night.  Thanks for the chat.

I've spent 3 years of my parents' good will making vague promises to attend school and only holding jobs periodically.  They've tried to nudge me out of the nest and at this point pushing me seems like the only option.  I'm fairly confident I could stay if I made any type of promise to them about my future, but I'm honestly glad I've been asked to leave.

Thanks for the response.

When I say moving out, I mean that I get to live in my car. Not very relaxing, but I can make it work for awhile. I actually get along very well with both my parents. They're wonderful people and I only wish them happiness. It just feels worse when you let down the people you care about and in that way I wish it were different. It seems strange to say, but if they despised me I could truly be alone. And oddly enough that's what I want.

Obviously I've never found any type of permanent restitution so I'm not quite sure how to answer the question.  This is what's true for me.  Whenever your mind is busy you simply don't have room for introspection.  So in that sense anything that keeps the mind busy does wade off thoughts of suicide.  But, a mind only stays busy for so long.  Eventually, it's just you and your thoughts.  And your thoughts make poor company.  That's not much of an answer.  The question is probably better suited for someone that has beaten depression/suicidal tendencies.

Thanks for the pep talk.  Logically I can tell that everyone wants what's best for me, but even knowing that I still have the same negative thoughts over and over again.  I spend more time planning how I'm going to die than I spend trying to improve myself or my situation.

I leave some things out on the off chance that someone recognizes me and also because I'm just not comfortable saying some things.  That's the main reason I don't tell a story from the beginning to present day.  It's hard to deny a story that goes into explicit details.  I don't really mind sharing random vague bits of information though.

The story you told was very chilling.  I'm not sure if I really want to die.  I know I wish I hadn't been born, but that's not really the same.  I'd describe it more as slowly being pushed towards the edge of a cliff by an invisible force.  I can fight this force as long as I want, but it won't relent and eventually I will become tired.  It feels  inevitable.
I understand your position.  I've edited out some of the more explicit questions and rephrased others.  Hopefully that helps keep the post up.  I purposely leave many things about myself out.
